units.sourceHTML: Storing C Data
units.originalInnerHTML: Storing C Data

units.sourceHTML:
An embedded language often needs to work with native data. You may want a
pointer to some memory managed in the C heap, or maybe you want to store a chunk
of data more efficiently than Wren’s dynamism allows. You may want a Wren object
that represents a native resource like a file handle or database connection.
units.originalInnerHTML:
An embedded language often needs to work with native data. You may want a
pointer to some memory managed in the C heap, or maybe you want to store a chunk
of data more efficiently than Wren’s dynamism allows. You may want a Wren object
that represents a native resource like a file handle or database connection.

units.sourceHTML: For those cases, you can define a foreign class, a chimera whose state is half Wren and half C. It is a real Wren class with a name, constructor, and methods. You can define methods on it written in Wren, or foreign methods written in C. It produces real Wren objects that you can pass around, do ⟦CODE0⟧ checks on, etc. But it also wraps a blob of raw memory that is opaque to Wren but accessible from C.
units.originalInnerHTML: For those cases, you can define a foreign class, a chimera whose state is half Wren and half C. It is a real Wren class with a name, constructor, and methods. You can define methods on it written in Wren, or foreign methods written in C. It produces real Wren objects that you can pass around, do is checks on, etc. But it also wraps a blob of raw memory that is opaque to Wren but accessible from C.

class is through other foreign methods. Those are usually defined on the same
foreign class, but can be defined on other classes as well. Wren doesn’t care.

units.sourceHTML: Freeing Resources #
units.originalInnerHTML: Freeing Resources #

units.sourceHTML:
If your foreign instances are just holding memory and you’re OK with Wren’s
garbage collector managing the lifetime of that memory, then you’re done. Wren
will keep the bytes around as long as there is still a reference to them. When
the instance is no longer reachable, eventually the garbage collector will do
its thing and free the memory.
units.originalInnerHTML:
If your foreign instances are just holding memory and you’re OK with Wren’s
garbage collector managing the lifetime of that memory, then you’re done. Wren
will keep the bytes around as long as there is still a reference to them. When
the instance is no longer reachable, eventually the garbage collector will do
its thing and free the memory.

units.sourceHTML:
But, often, your foreign data refers to some resource whose lifetime needs to
be explicitly managed. For example, if you have a foreign object that wraps an
open file handle, you need to ensure that handle doesn’t get left open when the
GC frees the foreign instance.
units.originalInnerHTML:
But, often, your foreign data refers to some resource whose lifetime needs to
be explicitly managed. For example, if you have a foreign object that wraps an
open file handle, you need to ensure that handle doesn’t get left open when the
GC frees the foreign instance.

units.sourceHTML:
Of course, you can (and usually should) add a method on your foreign class, like
⟦CODE0⟧ so the user can explicitly release the resource managed by the object.
But if they forget to do that and the object is no longer reachable, you want to
make sure the resource isn’t leaked.
units.originalInnerHTML: Of course, you can (and usually should) add a method on your foreign class, like close() so the user can explicitly release the resource managed by the object. But if they forget to do that and the object is no longer reachable, you want to make sure the resource isn’t leaked.

units.sourceHTML: To that end, you can also provide a finalizer function when binding the foreign class. That’s the other callback in the WrenForeignClassMethods struct. If you provide that callback, then Wren will invoke it when an instance of your foreign class is about to be freed by the garbage collector. This gives you one last chance to clean up the object’s resources.
units.originalInnerHTML: To that end, you can also provide a finalizer function when binding the foreign class. That’s the other callback in the WrenForeignClassMethods struct. If you provide that callback, then Wren will invoke it when an instance of your foreign class is about to be freed by the garbage collector. This gives you one last chance to clean up the object’s resources.

units.sourceHTML:
Because this is called during the middle of a garbage collection, you do not
have unfettered access to the VM. It’s not like a normal foreign method where
you can monkey around with slots and other stuff. Doing that while the GC is
running could leave Wren in a weird state.

have unfettered access to the VM. It’s not like a normal foreign method where
